requestLimits.description: Request body limits at the ingress, matching the upload limits of docs/api.md. Owned by issue #82 alone: it fills this property and templates/_requestlimits.tpl.

replicaCount.description: cmd/solobill's session store is in-memory (govue's session.NewMemoryStore), and so is the passkey challenge store; both are correct for exactly one replica. A second replica would keep its own, separate set of sessions, so a request load-balanced to the other pod would see its caller as logged out.

adminPort.description: The administrative container port cmd/solobill serves /metrics, /healthz and /readyz on through govue's httpserver.RunAdmin. Must match config.adminListenAddr. Deliberately a field of its own, not under service: it is exposed on the Service as its own named port (see templates/service.yaml), but the Ingress still only ever routes to service.port; see values.yaml's own comment for why.

name.description: Name of the Gateway this HTTPRoute attaches to. Required when httpRoute.enabled is true; enforced by a template fail guard, not minLength, matching this chart's existing pattern for a value with no usable default.

namespace.description: Namespace the Gateway lives in. Required when httpRoute.enabled is true; see parentRefs.name's own description.

networkPolicy.description: A NetworkPolicy over this chart's own pods. It has no effect at all on a cluster whose CNI does not implement NetworkPolicy: such a cluster stores the object without error or warning and enforces none of it. See README.md's 'NetworkPolicy' section.

public.description: Scopes who may reach service.port. namespaceSelector and podSelector are each a plain label map (a matchLabels block), not the full Kubernetes LabelSelector shape, and go into one peer, so they are ANDed; ipBlock is its own peer, ORed with them, because the API rejects a peer carrying both. Every selector empty, the default, admits any source on that port, since an ingress controller or Gateway lives in a cluster-owned namespace this chart cannot name in advance.

admin.description: Scopes who may reach adminPort (/metrics, /healthz, /readyz). Same shape as public above. Every selector empty, the default, admits nothing: the rule is omitted entirely, which is the only way to deny a port, since an ingress rule with ports and no 'from' means any source per the NetworkPolicy API. Kubelet probe traffic needs nothing here, originating from the node.

egress.description: The egress half of the policy, with its own flag: it is the half whose mistakes break an installation rather than expose one, so it can be dropped while the admin-port isolation stays.

dns.description: Destination scope for the DNS egress rule, on top of its port restriction. Both selectors default to a non-empty value (kube-system / k8s-app: kube-dns). Helm merges an override into a default map key by key, and matchLabels ANDs the result, so an override under a different key is added alongside the default rather than replacing it: null the specific default key to replace it, or null the whole selector (not {}, which Helm merges into the default) to drop it.

postgres.description: PostgreSQL egress. port is explicit rather than parsed out of config.databaseUrl, and templates/networkpolicy.yaml fails the render when the two name different ports. Every selector empty, the default, admits any destination on that port: config.databaseUrl may name a database outside this cluster, which no selector can describe. Use ipBlock for that case.

oidc.description: Identity provider egress, rendered only while config.oidc.issuerUrl is set. Same shape and the same render-time port guard as postgres above.

objectStore.description: The S3 compatible store for receipts, imported originals and the logo. Owned by issue #75 alone, together with templates/_objectstore.tpl and templates/files-verify-cronjob.yaml.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the S3 API, scheme and host only: http or https, no user info, path, query or fragment. Empty: no store, the file routes answer 503. Checked by a template fail guard in templates/_objectstore.tpl, not a schema pattern: helm prints a rejected value in a schema error, and an error text must never carry a URL.

adminListenAddr.description: ADMIN_LISTEN_ADDR. Must match adminPort. /metrics, /healthz and /readyz are served here, never on listenAddr; see adminPort's own description.

databaseUrl.description: Credential-free Postgres connection URL (scheme, host, port, database, query parameters only). Required: templates/deployment.yaml fails the render with a readable message when this is empty, rather than this schema rejecting it with a cryptic minLength error. The role named by databaseUser MUST be NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS: db/migrations relies on FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY for tenant isolation, which a superuser or BYPASSRLS role bypasses regardless of FORCE.

databaseUser.description: Postgres role solobill connects as. Required; see databaseUrl's own description for why this is enforced by a template fail guard, not minLength. MUST be NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS, provisioned that way by the cluster operator: a superuser or BYPASSRLS role bypasses every row-level-security policy this application depends on for tenant isolation, silently and regardless of FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

loginRateLimits.description: The limits in front of the routes that verify a password, a TOTP code or a passkey. 0 and an empty string keep cmd/solobill's defaults.

passkey.description: The WebAuthn relying party. Passkeys are off while rpId is empty. Configuration only, never derived from a request.

name.description: Name of the existing Secret, created by the cluster's own secret manager operator, carrying every key below. This chart never creates this Secret from plaintext values. Required: templates/deployment.yaml fails the render with a readable message when this is empty, rather than this schema rejecting it with a cryptic minLength error.

databasePasswordKey.description: Key for DATABASE_PASSWORD. Required. The role this password authenticates MUST be NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS; see config.databaseUser's own description.

migrationDatabasePasswordKey.description: Password key for migrationJob.databaseUser, in this same Secret. Left empty, falls back to databasePasswordKey.

databaseUser.description: Separate role that owns and migrates the schema, distinct from config.databaseUser. No usable default: templates/deployment.yaml fails the render, not this schema with minLength, when this is left empty or set equal to config.databaseUser while migrationJob.enabled is true, matching config.databaseUrl/config.databaseUser/existingSecret.name's own pattern. See values.yaml's own comment and README.md's 'One role, or two' section.
